rename.to: location.go() doesn't notify the location.subscribe subject

body:
We are listening to [popstate event](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/%40angular/platform-browser/src/browser/location/browser_platform_location.ts#L45) which should be triggered by [history.pushState](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/modules/%40angular/platform-browser/src/browser/location/browser_platform_location.ts#L59) but according to https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WindowEventHandlers/onpopstate :
> Note that just calling history.pushState() or history.replaceState() won't trigger a popstate event. The popstate event is only triggered by doing a browser action such as clicking on the back button (or calling history.back() in JavaScript). And the event is only triggered when the user navigates between two history entries for the same document.

I'm getting "Property 'pushState' does not exist on type 'Location'."

is this fix just waiting for approval?
i'm also expecting a changed state after location.go().  where can i listen to these events?
... you have to wait for PR https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/19463 which is still just only on the master.

As @DzmitryShylovich pointed out in https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/12691#issuecomment-264697166, this relates to the `popState` event not triggering. `onUrlChange` should be used instead https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-router-base-17kggk?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.ts

This behavior is somewhat documented 
https://angular.io/api/common/Location#onurlchange
https://angular.io/api/common/Location#subscribe
but could use some revision to better address user expectations.
Docs team can refer to the material in this issue to update the API docs.

issue.body:
This PR changes the logic for determining when to skip route processing from
using the URL of the last attempted navigation to the actual resulting URL after
that transition.

Because guards may prevent navigation and reset the browser URL, the raw
URL of the previous transition may not match the actual URL of the
browser at the end of the navigation process. For that reason, we need to use
`urlAfterRedirects` instead.

Other notes:
* These checks in `scheduleNavigation` were added in https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/eb2ceff4ba19a09a5f400f81e371ec176878cd37
The test still passes and, more surprisingly, passes if the checks are removed
completely. There have likely been changes to the navigation handling that
handle the test in a different way. That said, it still appears to be important
to keep the checks there in some capacity because it does affect how many
navigation events occur. 
* This addresses an issue that came up in #16710: https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/16710#issuecomment-634869739
* This also partially addresses #13586 in fixing history for imperative
navigations that are cancelled by guards.

issue.body:
`Location.go` does not trigger the browser's `popstate` event because
the Angular Router uses `pushState` and `replaceState`. This can be
confusing when calling `Location.go` and using `Location.subscribe`.
This commit clarifies the behavior of `Location.subscribe` and points
developers to the `onUrlChanges` subscription instead.

Fixes #12691
